title: Streaming reference-probe watch and staged auto-revert for model rollouts
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Goal: Build a streaming 'reference-probe' watch that continuously evaluates canary and shadow traffic against tenant-scoped reference prompt sets (golden seeds) and enforces cohort-weighted gating with temporal hysteresis to reduce flapping. The system should be able to alert, quarantine, and perform staged auto-reverts when quality regressions cross configurable thresholds for a given customer cohort or global rollout.

Background: Current canary rollouts rely on periodic batch evals and coarse scorecard alerts. That causes delayed detection and manual rollback work. We need a real-time quality guard that integrates with the Console rollouts controller, uses streaming diffs from shadow traffic, and applies multi-metric scorecards (semantic similarity, token-level divergence, safety heuristics) with weighted thresholds per cohort.

Scope:
- Implement a streaming probe pipeline that samples shadow and canary responses and evaluates them against tenant-scoped and global reference prompt sets (managed in storage).
- Compute composite scorecards in near real-time using precomputed embeddings + lightweight syntactic checks.
- Support cohort weighting (by traffic slice, feature flag, and tenant) and configurable hysteresis windows (e.g., 5 minute lookback + cooldown) to prevent noisy autoreverts.
- Integrate alerting hooks into Console (per-route dashboards) and automate staged auto-revert via Rollout API with rollback policies (soft quarantine -> partial revert -> full revert).
- Provide a simulation harness to run historical traffic through the probe to calibrate thresholds before enabling on live rollouts.

Success criteria:
- Detect injected regressions (synthetic) with >= 95% recall and <= 2% false positive rate during 1-hour canary window for targeted cohorts.
- End-to-end autoscale revert completes within SLO: detection->revert < 3 minutes for high-severity regressions.
- Console surfaces per-customer probe metrics and a 'health score' for any active rollout.

Design notes & trade-offs:
- Streaming probe uses asynchronous sampling to avoid adding tail latency to inference paths: a per-request sampler forwards copy of response to probe stream.
- For scale, heavy evals (long semantic diffs / long-context metrics) run in batching workers; quick heuristics (token churn, safety flags, embedding similarity) run inline in the probe stream.
- Tenant-scoped golden sets reduce noise but require lifecycle management (uploading, vetting). We'll provide a UI + API for customer-specific golden seeds, but default to curated global seeds.
- Hysteresis parameters are tunable; conservative defaults recommended to prioritize availability over aggressive autoreverts.

Implementation plan:
1) Probe ingest and sampling: add sampler hook to serving runtime (ENG change) that writes to probe Kafka topic.
2) Lightweight probe worker: stream processor that computes quick score metrics and emits per-event signals.
3) Composite scorecard service: aggregates signals over sliding window, applies cohort weights and threshold logic.
4) Rollout orchestration: extend Rollout API to accept probe signals and implement staged auto-revert policies.
5) Console integration: probe metrics UI, alert rules, and an enable/disable toggle per-release.
6) Simulation harness: replay historical traffic and synthetic perturbations to tune thresholds.

Telemetry & observability:
- New metrics: probe.sample_rate, probe.latency_ms, probe.false_positives, probe.true_positives, scorecard.health, revert_latency_ms.
- Dashboards: per-model and per-route heatmaps; per-cohort time series; recent revert audit log.
- Audit: every auto-revert creates an immutable incident record with links to sampled probes and the synthetic golden comparison used.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: noisy golden sets cause unwarranted rollbacks. Mitigation: tiered rollout (shadow-only -> advisory -> auto-revert) and require manual opt-in for aggressive auto-reverts.
- Risk: scale/cost of continuous evaluations. Mitigation: adaptive sampling and fallbacks to cheaper heuristics; offload heavy evals to batch workers.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end smoke runs in staging with synthetic regressions demonstrate revert < 3 minutes.
- Simulation harness accurately maps threshold -> FP/TP tradeoff and recommended defaults checked in PR.
- Console shows live probe metrics and rollback operations are reflected in audit logs.
- Security review for tenant golden upload flow completed.

comments: 2026-02-10 - Aisha Kaur: Created ticket. Initial design drafted and linked. Prefers staged auto-revert with quarantine lane rather than immediate full revert.

2026-02-18 - Marcus Liu: Spike complete — sampler hook implemented in runtime branch spike/probe-sampler. Observed <0.5ms p50 additional latency when sampling 1% of traffic. See PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/rw-runtime/pull/898
2026-02-23 - Sofia Ortega (PM): Requested cohort-weighting feature to support enterprise customers with stricter SLAs. Added project label. Asked for simulation harness before canary enablement.

2026-03-02 - Marcus Liu: Prototype scorecard service up in staging. Using embedding-based similarity + token churn. Early tests show good signal for semantic regressions, some noise on safety heuristics — tuning in progress.

2026-03-05 - Security team (note): Need to complete review for tenant golden upload API. Raised two concerns about role-based access and virus-scanning of uploaded artifacts. Assigned to security tracker SEC-1289.

2026-03-10 - Aisha Kaur: Design decision - default auto-revert mode set to 'soft' (partial traffic quarantine) for first 6 weeks post-launch. Customers can opt into aggressive auto-revert via feature flag.

2026-03-12 - Marcus Liu: Integrated with Rollout API PR #614; staged revert flow (quarantine -> 50% revert -> full) implemented in controller. End-to-end smoke tests in staging passed; moving to canary on low-risk model tomorrow. Blocker cleared: storage lifecycle for tenant goldens addressed in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/golden-store/pull/37
